learning_objective: 🧫 Explore how animal cells are grown outside the body to create life-saving vaccines, test drugs, and produce antibodies!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Animal cells are much harder to grow than plant cells. They require complex media enriched with Fetal Bovine Serum (FBS), strict temperature control (37°C), and a CO2 incubator (usually 5%) to maintain the pH of the medium.

Primary cultures are directly from animal tissue and have a limited lifespan (Hayflick limit) due to contact inhibition. Continuous cell lines are often derived from cancer cells (like HeLa cells); they lose contact inhibition and can divide indefinitely.

Invented by Kohler and Milstein. They fused a normal antibody-producing B-cell (which dies quickly) with a myeloma cancer cell (which lives forever) to create a 'Hybridoma'. This cell continuously pumps out identical (monoclonal) antibodies.

Many viral vaccines (like Polio, Rabies, and Chickenpox) cannot be grown in bacterial broth because viruses need host cells. They are cultured on massive scales using animal cell lines (like Vero cells derived from monkey kidneys).
Instead of testing cosmetics or drugs on live animals, companies can use animal cell cultures in a petri dish. This is more ethical, faster, and cheaper.

fun_activity.title: 🧬 The Immortal Henrietta Lacks
fun_activity.instructions: Search the story of 'HeLa cells'. In 1951, cancer cells were taken from a woman named Henrietta Lacks without her knowledge. These cells never died and became the first immortal human cell line. They have since been used in space research, polio vaccine development, and thousands of cancer studies worldwide!

exam_tips: 📌 Distinguish clearly between anchorage-dependent cells (most normal cells that need a surface to grow on) and anchorage-independent cells (like blood cells or cancer cells that float).
📌 Hybridoma technology is a guaranteed question. Remember the fusion: B-cell + Myeloma cell = Hybridoma (for Monoclonal Antibodies).
📌 Explain the role of CO2 in incubators: It reacts with bicarbonate in the media to act as a buffer, keeping the pH stable.
quick_recap: ⭐ The 'Hayflick Limit' is the number of times a normal human cell population will divide before cell division stops (around 50 times).
⭐ Proteolytic enzymes like Trypsin are used to detach adherent cells from the bottom of the culture flask for subculturing.
⭐ Monoclonal antibodies are used extensively in modern medicine, including targeted cancer therapies and home pregnancy tests.
